{{Quote|Wicket! The Quorks are sworn enemies of the Ewoks! And if they ever learn how to hang glide&hellip;''"''<br />''"''I said we'd make him a glider, Teebo! I didn't say it would fly!|Teebo learns of Wicket W. Warrick's plan to dupe the king of the Quorks|<ref name="E3" />}}
The '''Quorks''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]], [[Hair/Legends|furry]], horned [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] found on the [[Forest/Legends|Forest]] [[Moon/Legends|Moon]] of [[Endor/Legends|Endor]]. They were burly creatures known more for brawn than [[Brain/Legends|brains]]. Nevertheless, they were apt warriors who employed wooden and stone weapons as well as domesticated [[devil beast]]s against their foes. The Quorks inhabited [[Quork City]] and were ruled by a [[King/Legends|king]]. They were sworn enemies of Endor's native [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]].

Circa [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the Quork King [[Marlox]] laid a trap for the Ewoks of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]], who came each [[Standard year/Legends|year]] to harvest [[sacred wood]] to make [[Hang-glider/Legends|hang gliders]]. The Quorks captured three Ewoks, and the King compelled two of them to construct a glider for him lest their friend be given to a devil beast to eat. However, the Ewoks escaped while the Quorks fought over who would be the first to use the completed flying machine. When Marlox pursued them in his new conveyance, he learned that it had been built to fall apart. The glider collapsed around him, and the Ewoks stole off with the sacred wood.

==Biology and appearance==
{{Quote|Almost finished! I just hope these Quorks are as stupid as they look!|Wicket W. Warrick prepares to spring his trap for the king of the Quorks|<ref name="E3" />}}
[[File:Strong_Quorks.png|thumb|left|Quorks were strong enough to carry large bundles of wood one-armed.]]
Quorks were stocky, [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] covered in shaggy, tangled [[Hair/Legends|fur]].<ref name="CSWE III 65">{{CSWECite|III|65|Quork}}</ref> Their hair was [[Color/Legends|brown]] all over except on the head, where a white mane framed the hairless, pale-colored face. The hands and feet were hairless as well. Their [[Limb/Legends|legs]] were short and their arms long in proportion to the body. They had four digits on every extremity, each sporting a hard nail.<ref name="E3" /> Members of the [[Species/Legends|species]] stood around 1.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall on average<ref name="height" /> and were heavily muscled. One Quork, for example, could carry a large bundle of wood one-handed.<ref name="E3" />

In the opinion of the [[Endor/Legends|Forest Moon of Endor's]] [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]], Quorks smelled foul and appeared unintelligent. Members of the species had large, wide-set [[Nose/Legends|nostrils]], a wide [[Mouth/Legends|mouth]], and thick brow ridges&mdash;covered in scraggly black eyebrows&mdash;over the [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]. Their snaggle-[[Tooth/Legends|teeth]] were large and sharp, and their two short, pointed, yellow or pink horns were on top of the head.<ref name="E3" />

==Society and culture==
{{Quote|Rope the beast! Get Ewok! Ewok!|Quork battle cries|<ref name="E3" />}}
[[File:QuorkCity.png|thumb|right|The Quorks of Endor lived in Quork City.]]
Quorks were quarrelsome beings concerned with personal status and power.<ref name="E3" /> By [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="Date">{{InsiderCite|23|Star Wars Publications Timeline|''Star Wars'' Publications Timeline}} dates the events of the [[Star Wars: Ewoks (1985)|''Ewoks'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]], which include the events of [[Ewoks (1985) 3|''Ewoks'' 3]], to three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] after the events of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which corresponds to [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] according to ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> Quorks on the [[Forest/Legends|Forest]] [[Moon/Legends|Moon]] of Endor had founded a settlement called [[Quork City]], which was under the rule of a [[King/Legends|king]]. The [[City/Legends|city]] was located on a cliff<ref name="E3" /> in a canyon-shrouded valley<ref name="CSWE III 65" /> near the grove where the Ewoks of [[Bright Tree Village/Legends|Bright Tree Village]] gathered the [[sacred wood]] from which they built their [[Hang-glider/Legends|hang gliders]]. In that population center, the Quorks constructed hive-shaped homes of stone with open doorways and [[Window/Legends|windows]]. A few buildings had multiple stories, although most were no taller than ground level. The king ruled from a room where his yellow, stone throne was located. He was distinguished from other members of his species by his golden [[Crown/Legends|crown]].<ref name="E3" /> Most members of the species were [[Hunting/Legends|hunters]] and gatherers.<ref name="CSWE III 65" />

Endor's Quorks lived at a relatively low level of technology.<ref name="CSWE III 65" /> By 3 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]],<ref name="Date" /> they had trained a [[devil beast]] to help capture [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]]. They constructed tools from stone and wood, including [[cart]]s that rolled on wooden wheels, cloth that hung from doorways, and knotted [[Rope/Legends|ropes]] that could subdue a devil beast. The Quork king had [[Glass/Legends|glass]] containers of victuals and [[Wax/Legends|wax]] [[Candle/Legends|candles]] in his throne room. [[Fruit/Legends|Fruits]] were among the items that made up the species' diet.<ref name="E3" />

The Quorks of Endor were adept at warfare. They understood the importance of ambushing an enemy and attacking with the element of surprise. Quork warriors signaled an imminent attack with [[Drum/Legends|drums]] made of skin stretched across a hollow base and beaten with cloth-wrapped sticks. The species' warriors attacked with [[Spear/Legends|spears]], which were wielded in close combat and hurled at the enemy. These weapons were made from a wooden shaft attached by cord to a stone point. If the aim of a raid was to capture a living being, the Quorks tried to snag their target using rope lassos.<ref name="E3" />

Prisoners of war were marched on foot back to the Quorks' city. Ill treatment was commonplace, as the Ewok [[Wicket Wystri Warrick/Legends|Wicket Warrick]] discovered when his cries of defiance were met by the butt of a spear. Once within the city confines, prisoners were locked away in a [[Prison/Legends|prison]] that, unlike most Quork buildings, had a wooden door and wooden bars on the windows. There, [[Torture/Legends|torture]] by means of food and [[Water/Legends|water]] deprivation was an accepted practice.<ref name="E3" />

Endor's Quorks had sworn their enmity for Ewoks. In their eyes, Ewoks were simply another form of property to be taken at will. For their part, Ewoks held a dim view of the Quorks and considered them stupid<ref name="E3" /> and oafish. Nevertheless, the Quorks envied the Ewoks' advanced technology,<ref name="CSWE III 65" /> especially their hang gliders, and coveted the expertise to build similar vehicles for themselves.<ref name="E3" />

==History==
{{Quote|Who could've done such a horrible thing?''"<br />"''I don't know, but we Ewoks have been harvesting this wood for many years&hellip; so whoever did this must have known we would come here!|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka and Teebo discover that the Quorks have taken their sacred wood|<ref name="E3" />}}
[[File:Marlox.png|thumb|left|upright|Marlox was the king of the Quorks by the middle of 3 ABY.]]
A group of Quorks on the Forest Moon of Endor came to be the sworn enemies of the moon's native Ewoks.<ref name="E3" /> By mid-3 ABY,<ref name="Date" /> the Quorks had established Quork City, a population center situated where the moon's forest gave way to [[Mountain/Legends|mountains]]. A Quork named [[Marlox]] came to power as their king.<ref name="E3" />

From their base, the Quorks observed that a group of Ewoks traveled to the region on hang gliders and collected wood each year.<ref name="E3" /> Circa 3 ABY,<ref name="Date" /> however, the Quorks beat them to the grove and felled the forest first. A group of Quork warriors lay in wait for the Ewoks that would inevitably come. When a group of three did show up&mdash;[[Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka/Legends|Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka]], [[Teebo/Legends|Teebo]], and Wicket W. Warrick&mdash;the Quorks sprang their ambush as the new arrivals investigated the desolate landscape. The Ewoks managed to escape on their gliders, but the Quorks unleashed a devil beast that engaged the airborne Ewoks and snatched Warrick from his glider. With Ewok and sacred wood in tow, the Quorks returned to their home.<ref name="E3" />

Back in Quork City, King Marlox ordered the prisoner to construct a glider from the sacred wood. The Ewok refused and was cast into a prison cell, where he would be denied food and water until he complied. When the other Ewoks showed up in the city and attacked, the prisoner escaped. Nevertheless, the Quorks managed to gather all three Ewoks and throw them together into the prison. King Marlox threatened to turn the devil beast loose on Kintaka unless the other two Ewoks made him the glider he desired, and they agreed.<ref name="E3" />

Some time later, Warrick announced that the glider had been completed, but that only the smartest of Quorks could fly it. The information sparked a tussle between the Quorks over the privilege of taking the craft out for its maiden voyage, and the [[Gender/Legends|male]] Ewoks escaped. The king tried to give chase in his new glider, but it disintegrated immediately. Enraged that he had been tricked, King Marlox ordered the release of the devil beast.<ref name="E3" />

The male Ewoks took to their gliders and diverted the creature away from their tethered friend. The Ewok Teebo swooped low and cut Kintaka's bonds, and Warrick took her aboard his glider. Still being chased by the devil beast, the Ewoks swooped close to Marlox's throne room and caused the pursuing creature to crash into the king's hut. The Ewoks escaped on their gliders with the sacred wood in tow.<ref name="E3" />

{{Unlicensedstart}}
Later, Marlox and his Quorks captured Kneesaa a Jari Kintaka while she was away from her village collecting [[Sacred rock/Legends|sacred rocks]]. The Quork King placed the Princess in a [[Prison/Legends|cell]] to hold her as a bargaining chip in negotiations with her [[Parent/Legends|father]], [[Chief/Legends|Chief]] [[Chirpa/Legends|Chirpa]] of the Ewoks. Meanwhile, the Ewok Chief dispatched Wicket W. Warrick to find his missing daughter. Warrick infiltrated Quork City, where he overheard Marlox's plans to use Kintaka for ransom&mdash;Warrick speculated that the Quork King would try to trade her for the Ewoks' [[Shadowroot soap|invisibility soap]]. The [[Unidentified Quork guard 1|Quork]] [[Unidentified Quork guard 2|guards]] soon found themselves under attack as Warrick burst into the jail and freed his fellow Ewok. Marlox himself was prevented from stopping the Ewoks after Warrick threw sand in his face. The Quorks could only watch impotently as the Ewoks jumped off a nearby cliff and flew to safety on their hang gliders.<ref name="PiaP">{{StoryCite|story=The Princess in a Predicament|book=MyComyc|bformatted=''MyComyc'' 3}}</ref>
{{Unlicensedend}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|What's more, the writers clearly knew their source material,&hellip; working Teebo, Kneesaa, Chirpa, Logray, Paploo, Latara, Morag, the mantigrue, Gorneesh, and even the Quorks (from Marvel's issue #3) into ''Ewoks''.|Randy Stradley|<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/droids-and-ewoks-return-spains-lost-star-wars-comic-strips|text=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost ''Star Wars'' Comic Strips|int=Droids and Ewoks Return: Spain's Lost Star Wars Comic Strips|nolive=1}}</ref>}}
The Quorks feature as the major villains of the [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] [[Ewoks (1985) 3|''Ewoks'' 3]], written by [[David Manak]] and illustrated by [[Warren Kremer]]. The story was originally published in September [[1985]].<ref name="E3" /> The Quorks also feature in "[[The Princess in a Predicament]],"<ref name="PiaP" /> a [[Wikipedia:Spain|Spanish]] story that was published in [[1986]] under the ''[[MyComyc]]'' label. In the decades that followed their initial publication, the ''MyComyc'' strips were mostly forgotten, and were only rediscovered in [[2013]]. [[Randy Stradley]], Vice President of Publishing for [[Dark Horse Comics]], expressed interest in including the ''MyComyc'' strips in a future [[Star Wars Omnibus]] publication, but [[Lucasfilm]] found no formal proof that those titles were actually licensed, despite the presence of appropriate copyright information. Because of that uncertainty over licensing, "The Princess in a Predicament" and the events it relates are considered of ambiguous [[canon]]icity.<ref name="Blog" />
